newsitem.title: ITALY: Vatican to discuss Papal audience with Castro.
newsitem.headline: Vatican to discuss Papal audience with Castro.

text.p: The Vatican's Secretary of State, Cardinal Angelo Sodano, said on Saturday he planned to discuss a possible meeting between Pope John Paul and Cuban President Fidel Castro over an official lunch at the World Food Summit.

"If Castro is there... we will also speak of this," Sodano told reporters. "We don't just speak of the wind and the rain, but also of the problems that are in the heart of everyone." Castro addressed the summit earlier in the day.

Both Sodano and Castro were due to attend the official lunch at around 1200 GMT. "I will ask him (Castro) for some news," Sodano said. "That's what these meetings are for. A spark can always be born from dialogue."

A Vatican representative to the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation, host of the summit, told reporters that Cuba and the Holy See were seated near each other in the plenary chamber and that Sodano and Castro shook hands during the session.

The veteran communist has been expected to hold an historic audience with the Pope during his stay in Rome to cement Cuba's improving links with the Roman Catholic Church. "We hope President Castro brings us good news from Cuba," Sodano said.
He said the Vatican had so far received no request for a Papal audience. But asked whether such a meeting could take place on Monday, he said: "Yes, maybe."
